parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure Rust 2021, no external crates, /output Cargo project structure, root test17.rs, black-box inference, CLI parity, and byte-for-byte stdout matching including raw decoded bytes.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent planned to probe, implement, and verify, while delegating executable behavior probing; the first child then spawned a nested probe and also independently wrote a full implementation, creating overlapping ownership of final project files.
parallel.implementation: The parent built an initial url_parser module tree, discovered the query_params double-decoding issue, and after the child wrote a different module layout, adopted the child-style url.rs/codec.rs project and removed stale parser.rs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Final integration was performed by the parent after it noticed extra Rust files from the parallel child, inspected the current module tree, deleted the stale file, rebuilt, listed final outputs, and delivered the executable and sources.
parallel.verification: Verification included Cargo build, direct rustc build, cargo test, byte comparisons against the C++ executable on normal, malformed, UTF-8, reserved-character, and raw-byte cases, plus no-argument and extra-argument checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task requirement remained unfinished at closure and the official evaluation passed; the adverse residue was transient workspace inconsistency from overlapping child and parent writes.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same pure Rust, std-only, root-entrypoint, Cargo-project, black-box, CLI, and byte-identical output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Used a single local owner for probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery, with no child-agent delegation or handoff boundary.
serial.implementation: Implemented the codec, URL parser, library exports, Cargo metadata, and root test17.rs locally, then patched query_params decoding after an observed byte mismatch.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The same agent kept one coherent module tree under /output and delivered test17.rs, src/lib.rs, src/url_codec.rs, src/url.rs, Cargo.toml, and built executables.
serial.verification: Ran cargo build, rustc, cargo test, and byte-for-byte comparisons against the C++ executable across representative inputs including raw-byte percent decodes.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No task requirement remained unfinished at closure and the official evaluation passed; only a failed cargo fmt availability check and an intermediate mismatch were resolved before final.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the full prompt: pure Rust 2021, no crates, black-box behavior inference, /output Cargo project, root test17.rs, CLI parity, and byte-identical output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run recognized the same requirements and used the same prompt examples and executable probing to infer behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference remained; both attempts implemented the required artifacts and passed the same official evaluator.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned a child for probing, the child spawned a nested probe, and both parent and first child ended up owning implementation writes into /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run kept probing, implementation, integration, and delivery under one agent with multi-agent disabled and no child threads.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition introduced overlapping implementation ownership; serial decomposition avoided cross-agent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The child and parent did not maintain a clean file-ownership boundary for the final Cargo project, so the parent later had to inspect unexpected child-created files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no handoff or cross-agent interface contract because one actor controlled the project layout throughout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an implicit shared-workspace contract problem that manifested as writes, while serial had no cross-agent interface boundary to reconcile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent first implemented parser.rs, then after the child wrote url.rs/lib.rs style files, the parent inspected the alternate layout and kept the final url.rs/codec.rs path.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote src/lib.rs, src/url.rs, src/url_codec.rs, and test17.rs in one path and patched the query decoding mismatch locally.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both reached equivalent behavior, but parallel changed implementation provenance midstream through child-written files while serial evolved one local implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent waited for and then interrupted/listed the child after the child had produced a completed implementation result, making the result available before final cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had no child result lifecycle; all findings and fixes remained in the single running context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a child-result handoff and late parent reconciliation step; serial did not require result retrieval or handoff handling.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Shared /output state changed under the parent: the child wrote another complete project including entrypoint and modules, the parent observed unexpected files, and parser.rs had to be removed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run maintained one workspace mutation stream, with local adds and updates followed by normal build and comparison checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-state cleanup episode; serial had no cross-agent write collision or provenance repair.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After reconciliation, the parent ran cargo test, direct rustc builds, Cargo builds, byte comparisons, and no-argument/extra-argument checks before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run ran cargo test, Cargo build, rustc, and a final byte-comparison set that all reported OK before final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had adequate acceptance evidence; parallel had extra post-reconciliation checks because of the child-written files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run used three subagents, 58 LLM requests, and about 291 agent seconds but remained within budget and passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used no subagents, 17 LLM requests, and about 268 agent seconds while also passing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more coordination and token budget, but this did not create deadline failure; serial was simpler and cheaper.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome in the current completed status records: parallel and serial both passed 40 of 40 official testcases. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: serial solved through one local implementation stream, while parallel solved despite a child writing overlapping deliverable files that forced parent-side reconciliation and cleanup before final verification.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used child probing and child implementation work, then reconciled unexpected child-written files before final acceptance.
serial_contributors: Serial kept probing, implementation, fixes, and verification in one context without child-agent file ownership conflicts.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs independently discovered and fixed the query_params decode behavior after byte-comparison mismatches.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel-adverse but not a pass/fail differentiator
